concerns.location: tasks.md:Scope + T008 vs spec.md:FR-008, US-1/US-2 acceptance scenarios
concerns.text: Tasks narrow the study to N=100 per group while spec.md's acceptance scenarios and FR-008 explicitly require 500 scenes/prompts per group and a power analysis confirming N=500 yields power ≥0.8. T008 further weakens FR-008 to 'warn-and-continue if underpowered at N=100'. The N=100 staging is documented in plan/tasks but never reflected back into spec.md, so FR-008 and US-1/US-2 acceptance criteria are unsatisfiable as written — a silent requirement weakening. Either amend the spec (staged scope, deferred N=500) or restore spec-mandated N.

T012 states 'Research scripts must not write to state/ or modify platform state (platform owns artifact hashing)', directly contradicting the plan's Versioning Discipline compliance, which relies on code/utils/update_state.py writing SHA-256 hashes and updated_at into state/...yaml after each phase. One of the two must be corrected; as written, Constitution V has no implementing task.

Tasks introduce a third 'control' group (T003, T009 pairwise p-values including control) that spec.md never authorizes: FR-005 specifies a z-test on 'the two groups' and US-2's acceptance scenarios describe only baseline and experimental. The plan authorizes the control group, but the spec was never amended — the tasks implement scope the spec does not permit. Amend spec FR-005/US-2 to include the matched control group.

Spec edge case requires that images with detection confidence <0.7 be 'flagged for manual review' in addition to being conservatively counted as violations. T006 and the evaluation-result schema provide no manual-review flag or review artifact, so the flagging half of this compound requirement is silently dropped.

FR-007's 'tolerance for deviation of ≤ 1 pixel in bounding box coordinates' has no verification step in T004/T005 (seed_lock_status.json records mode but not the ≤1px tolerance check). FR-008's '[deferred]' effect size is filled in unilaterally as effect_size=0.2 in T008 with no traceable spec/plan decision — the parameter is untraceable and the spec requirement remains untestable as written.

Two conflicting physics-constraint schemas exist (YAML nested constraints/rule_type vs JSON flat object_a/object_b/relation, integer scene_id). T002 validates only against the YAML; the orphaned JSON contract should be removed or reconciled so an implementer cannot target the wrong schema.
